policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'a contentious and fretful woman' renders the noun as strife/contentions, which both the qere midyanim and the ketiv midonim yield; the only note is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, a contentious woman and vexation') and concerns English wording, not the reading. Nothing in the verse distinguishes the two spellings, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV text 'he establisheth his ways' renders yakin (ketiv), while the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, he considereth his way' records yabin (qere) as the rejected alternative. The ASV's own wording therefore selects the ketiv.

ASV text has the plural 'his ways' = derakaw (ketiv); the mapped textual_variant note gives the singular 'his way' = darko (qere) as the other reading. The plural in the text selects the ketiv, matching the same verse's yakin.
